parsed_payload.reasoning: The ten braid hyperplanes x_i=x_j divide R^5 into the 5! = 120 regions given by the strict orderings of the five coordinates. Add H_0: sum x_i = 0. For each ordering, choose x_{\pi(k)}=k-3; this preserves the ordering and has sum 0, so H_0 intersects every braid region and splits it into a sum>0 and a sum<0 part. The region count becomes 240. Add H_1: sum x_i = 1. This hyperplane is parallel to H_0 and lies entirely in the sum>0 half-space. It intersects each of the 120 sum>0 regions (for each ordering, shift the previous sum-0 choice by 1/5), but it cannot intersect any sum<0 region. Thus H_1 cuts exactly 120 regions, increasing the count to 360. Add H_{-1}: sum x_i = -1. It lies entirely in the sum<0 half-space, intersects each of the 120 sum<0 regions, and cuts exactly those, increasing the count to 480. Therefore the hyperplanes divide R^5 into \boxed{480} regions.
